title: AATIP, the DoD's UFO program, and its $22 million budget

tellings.quote: Just look at the main UFO program over the last 15 years out of the DoD. It's called ATIP or the Advanced Aerospace Threat Identification Program. ATIP has a $22 million budget.

That was until 2017 when a New York Times journalist named Leslie Kean revealed that the government had a UFO investigation program called AATIP that had formed in 2007 and was being run under the auspices of Bigelow Aerospace.
tellings.difference: Adds that Leslie Kean revealed the program in the New York Times in 2017 and that it ran under Bigelow Aerospace, and gives no $22 million budget.
tellings.link_reason: Both tellings are about AATIP, the US government UFO program formed in 2007. This one describes the program by way of its 2017 New York Times disclosure rather than a separate incident inside it.

tellings.quote: I was one of three journalists who broke the story in December of 2017 about the Department of Defense secret program studying UFOs
tellings.difference: This telling is in Kean's own first-person voice as one of three journalists who broke the story in December 2017. It does not name AATIP, Bigelow Aerospace or the $22 million budget.
tellings.link_reason: Both are about the DoD's secret UFO program (AATIP) being made public in the 2017 New York Times article that Leslie Kean co-wrote. The story already holds a telling about Kean revealing the program in 2017.

as_told.title: December 2017 story on the DoD's secret UFO program

tellings.quote: oap stands for the advanced Aerospace Weapons Systems application program a pentagon program that ran from 2007 to 2012
tellings.difference: Names the program AAWSAP rather than AATIP, ends it in 2012, credits Reid, Inouye and Stevens, and ties it to Skinwalker Ranch.
tellings.link_reason: Both describe the Pentagon UFO program that began in 2007, was run through Bigelow and had a $22 million budget.

tellings.quote: It's what Harry Reid set up from 2007 to 2012, this AATIP program, which then turned into sort of this ATIP overhang program which seemed a lot slimmer.
tellings.difference: Adds that AATIP later became a slimmer follow-on 'ATIP overhang' program, and gives no budget.
tellings.link_reason: This is the same DoD program Harry Reid set up and ran from 2007 to 2012, which the AATIP story already tells, crediting Reid.

tellings.quote: to say I ran this program it was actually under Senator Harry Reed who was interested in UFOs they had appropriated 22 million
tellings.difference: Puts the emphasis on Elizondo saying he ran the program, and mentions Skinwalker Ranch.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell of AATIP's $22 million funding through Harry Reid, with Stevens, Inouye and Bigelow involved.

as_told.title: Elizondo ran AATIP, funded with $22 million through Harry Reid

tellings.quote: Harry Reid, Senate Majority Leader uh on the Democratic side and representative in in Nevada, senator from Nevada, uh had funded $22 million along with I think Daniel Inway and Ted Stevens of Alaska uh to actually study UFOs in an official context.
tellings.difference: Emphasises Reid as the Senate Majority Leader from Nevada who secured the funding.
tellings.link_reason: Same $22 million DoD UFO study funded through Reid, Inouye and Stevens in 2007-2012.

as_told.title: Harry Reid secures $22 million to study UFOs

tellings.quote: okay we had you know an anomalous sighting at Nimttz in 2004 we studied this stuff on the order of $22 million at Skinwalker Ranch from 2007 to 2012
tellings.difference: Places the $22 million study at Skinwalker Ranch.
tellings.link_reason: The same $22 million 2007-2012 program, which the story's tellings also place under OSAP from 2007 to 2012.

tellings.quote: It also included details about the existence of Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid's UFO program named [music] OAP that ran from 2007 to 2012.
tellings.difference: Calls it Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid's program, named OAP, and says the 2017 NYT article revealed it.
tellings.link_reason: Both are the Pentagon UFO program behind Harry Reid (OSAP/AAWSAP/AATIP), run from 2007 to 2012.

tellings.quote: That's Lou Elizondo, former director of AATIP, the government's Advanced Aerospace Threat Identification Program, which studied UFOs from 2007 to 2012.
tellings.difference: Brief statement dating it 2007-2012 and naming Elizondo as former director, no budget.
tellings.link_reason: Host describes AATIP as a UFO program run 2007-2012 with Elizondo; matches the AATIP program story.

related.note: The same $22 million Reid-funded program run through Bigelow Aerospace. The telling's core claim is new: Colonel Alexander set it up and steered it toward a fixed end, which the story's tellings do not say.

This is about the same 2007-2017 Pentagon program Elizondo was part of (AATIP). But it claims the program's real purpose was building advanced weapons from recovered UFO technology, not studying UFOs.

plain: From 2007 to 2012 the Pentagon ran a secret UFO study that Michels calls AATIP, the Advanced Aerospace Threat Identification Program, set up by Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid of Nevada with Senators Daniel Inouye and Ted Stevens, with $22 million, run through Bigelow Aerospace, the private space company of Robert Bigelow, and doing some of its work at a ranch known for strange reports called Skinwalker Ranch. Michels tells this himself again and again, and says the program came to light in the New York Times article 'Glowing Auras and "Black Money": The Pentagon's Mysterious U.F.O. Program', published on 16 December 2017, which the journalist Leslie Kean, in a clip, says she was one of three reporters to break. In some versions he calls it AAWSAP, the Advanced Aerospace Weapons System Applications Program, names the former intelligence official Luis Elizondo as its director, and says it later shrank into a slimmer follow-on; if true, Congress paid for an official UFO study years before the public was told.
